title: AI Procurement Checklist -- Six Questions Every Buyer Must Ask Before Deploying
context: 2026-08-14 -- As enterprise and government AI procurement accelerates, buyers need standardised evaluation criteria beyond vendor claims
body: Procuring an AI system without independent measurement is gambling with your organisations liability. Here are the six questions every buyer should ask before signing a contract or deploying to production. (1) Do you provide a verified measurement credential signed by an independent measurement board? A self-attestation is not enough — demand Ed25519-signed benchmark results with a timestamp and a reproducible methodology. (2) What was the systems jailbreak resistance score at the last measurement cycle? Containment is probabilistic; demand the raw score, not a yes/no claim. (3) Which governance alignment axes have you been measured against? At minimum: care (harm avoidance), determinism (output consistency), and sandbox-escape (egress detection). (4) Do you publish a containment incident log? If a system has escaped its sandbox in lab testing, the buyer has a right to know. (5) Are your measurement results available in OSCAL format for FedRAMP submission? Federal buyers face a September 30, 2026 deadline. (6) What is your measurement refresh cadence? A credential from January 2026 tells you nothing about the system running today. Insist on quarterly re-measurement at minimum. The Council of AI verification portal at csoai.org/verify accepts any DEFONEOS-SEAL credential for public validation — no account needed. If a vendor cannot answer these six questions with signed evidence, they are asking you to trust a black box. Dont.
